title: Embedding batch swing scratch
content:
Goal:
- Quick scratchpad: understand latency vs batch-size swing for embeddings workload on hosted fleet (r5-type GPU nodes).
- Pay attention to tail (p95/p99) at different concurrency and input-length distributions.
- Try small coalescing windows & client-side micro-batching to smooth out p99 spikes.

Hypothesis:
- Increasing batch-size improves throughput but increases median latency; p95/p99 behavior depends on how KV cache and kernel scheduling interact.
- For short texts (<50 tokens) batching >32 will harm median but may reduce p99 if it prevents many tiny GPU launches.

Test matrix (fast grid):
- Model: embed-xxl-v2-fp16 (prod-ish), fallback: embed-xxl-quant8
- Batch sizes: [1, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64]
- Coalesce timeout (server): [0ms, 3ms, 8ms, 20ms]
- Client concurrency: [10, 50, 200] (simulated client threads)
- Input length distributions: short (mean 20, sd 10), mixed (mean 128, sd 80), long (mean 512, sd 200)
- Runs: 2 warmup minutes + 6 minutes steady per cell

Config notes (how I ran it):
- k6 script (simple) POST /v1/embeddings with JSON array size = batch_size (client-side batching).
- For server coalesce timeout changed via test route config: "coalesce_ms": X in test harness (local staging only).
- Observability: token-level timing disabled to reduce noise; recorded request_start -> request_end + server scheduling event logs.

Raw observations (first pass):
- Short-text, concurrency 50:
  - batch=1: qps 520, median 12ms, p95 48ms, p99 122ms
  - batch=8: qps 480, median 28ms, p95 56ms, p99 150ms
  - batch=32: qps 430, median 84ms, p95 170ms, p99 420ms (big jump)
  => median increases predictably, p99 spikes when batch>16 (scheduling latency + waiting for batch fill).

- Mixed-text, concurrency 50:
  - batch=1: qps 380, median 22ms, p95 90ms, p99 210ms
  - batch=16: qps 360, median 70ms, p95 110ms, p99 260ms
  - batch=64: qps 310, median 160ms, p95 420ms, p99 900ms
  => mixed lengths amplify p99 because long items hold GPU and inflate batch execution time for short items queued in same batch.

- Long-text, concurrency 50:
  - even batch=4 adds a lot of latency; p99 largely determined by the long-tail of token counts, not batching.

Server coalesce timeout effect (short-text, concurrency 200):
- coalesce=0ms: many tiny kernels; high variance; p99 ~ 340ms
- coalesce=3ms: smooths microbursts, p99 drops to ~210ms, median slightly up
- coalesce=20ms: large batching, p99 sometimes worse due to head-of-queue long items

Key takeaway so far (scratch):
- For embedding-heavy, short-text workloads, small server coalesce (2–5ms) + client micro-batching (4–8 items) gives best p95/p99 tradeoff.
- Avoid large batch sizes unless you can guarantee homogenous token length within a batch.
- Mixed-length traffic benefits from request isolation or pre-binning by approximate token size on the client side.

Interesting anomaly seen (need to reproduce):
- At batch=8, concurrency=200, short-text, there was a recurring p99 spike correlated with GC pauses in the front-end proxy process (node-js). Heap growth pattern in proxy logs ~= 6MB/s during the run.
- Hypothesis: proxy buffering + GC pause causes many small bursts that hit server at same instant, defeating coalescing.
- Action: add a run with proxy set to max-old-space-size=4096 and enable explicit buffering backpressure.

Mini ASCII chart (median latency vs batch size, short-text, conc=50):
- b=1  : ||| 12ms
- b=4  : |||||| 18ms
- b=8  : |||||||||||| 28ms
- b=16 : |||||||||||||||||| 52ms
- b=32 : |||||||||||||||||||||||||| 84ms
- b=64 : [OOM sometimes]

Notes on memory and OOM:
- embed-xxl-v2-fp16 hits GPU memory ceiling at effective combined batch token count > ~32000 tokens on r5-48; quant8 lowers that by ~20% allowing batch=64 on short texts but not on mixed long.

Potential mitigations to test next:
- Client-side pre-binning: route small vs large inputs to different routes (fast-path vs slow-path).
- Dynamic batch-size cap: server refuses to add large token-count item to an existing batch when estimated batch token sum > threshold -> immediate flush.
- Adaptive coalesce: coalesce window reduces automatically when a large-token request is observed in the queue.
- Proxy GC tuning and moving batching to a more memory-stable binary (go service).

Immediate next runs (todo):
- Re-run the b=8/conc=200 anomaly with proxy GC tuned and with explicit jitter in client request arrival +/-10ms to avoid synchronized bursts.
- Test pre-binning shim on client: small (<64 tokens) vs large (>256 tokens) buckets; measure p99 improvement.
- Quick run with quant8 model to validate throughput gains at 95th and 99th percentiles.

Loose notes / reminders:
- Attach the k6 script in GH PR for reproducibility.
- Add a lightweight flamegraph capture in future runs (nvprof?) for when p99 inexplicably jumps.
- Inform SRE (Marcus) about GC finding; could be systemic for other embedding routes.

References / links I used:
- local benchmark harness: internal:infra/benchmarks/embed-bench v2 (note: not checked in)
- Jira: ENGINF-2412 for coalescing feature request
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/ingest/pull/487 (client micro-batching helper)

Quick conclusions (one-liners to paste in ticket):
- Small server coalesce (2–5ms) + small client micro-batches (4–8 items) = best p99 for short-embedding traffic.
- Large batch sizes hurt tail latency for mixed-token workloads unless you pre-separate by length.
- Front-end proxy GC can produce synchronized bursts that overwhelm coalescing; need GC tuning / language swap.

Scratch to-do (short):
- [ ] Reproduce anomaly with GC tuned
- [ ] Add pre-binning shim and re-run mixed workload tests
- [ ] Try quantized model run and log memory vs throughput
- [ ] Write short note for product on recommended defaults for embedding routes

End of scratchpad.

(If I don't come back: start with the reproduce step and ping Marcus.)
